title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 7–9). L is a set and Φ ⊂ P(L) is a family of subsets with support |Φ| = ∪Φ. Φ is called 'admissible' when two conditions hold:
(i) every x ∈ |Φ| lies in a smallest member A(x) of Φ;
(ii) every A ∈ Φ has non-empty 'open part' A° = A minus the union of the members of Φ strictly contained in A.
The pieces A° are then strata partitioning |Φ|. Φ is in bijection with them, and Φ is ordered by inclusion so that A is the closure of A°. This is the face-poset / Alexandrov-topology picture of a stratified 'figure'.
- An admissible subfamily Ψ ⊂ Φ is one that is closed downward: B ⊂ A, A ∈ Ψ, B ∈ Φ implies B ∈ Ψ.
- A subset of |Φ| is Φ-closed when it is a union of members of Φ and is downward saturated.

The proposition concerns two admissible families Φ, Ψ ⊂ P(L). The following are equivalent:
- (a) Φ ∪ Ψ is admissible and Φ, Ψ are closed admissible subfamilies of it.
- (b) Φ ∩ Ψ is closed in Φ and in Ψ, and |Φ| ∩ |Ψ| = |Φ ∩ Ψ|.
- (c) T = |Φ| ∩ |Ψ| is Φ-closed in |Φ| and Ψ-closed in |Ψ|, and for A ⊂ T one has A ∈ Φ iff A ∈ Ψ.
Such Φ, Ψ are then called 'compatible'. This is the condition for gluing two stratified figures along a common closed substratification.

This page proves b ⇒ c and starts c ⇒ a.

b ⇒ c.
- Since Φ∩Ψ is downward closed in Φ and in Ψ, |Φ∩Ψ| is closed in |Φ| and in |Ψ|.
- Let A ∈ Φ with A ⊂ |Φ| ∩ |Ψ| = |Φ∩Ψ|.
- By the preliminary criterion, A ⊂ ∪_{B∈Φ∩Ψ} B. Take x ∈ A° (non-empty by admissibility); then x lies in some B ∈ Φ∩Ψ.
- Minimality of A(x) = A gives A ⊂ B. Downward closedness of Φ∩Ψ in Φ then gives A ∈ Φ∩Ψ ⊂ Ψ.
- The symmetric statement holds the same way.

c ⇒ a, step 1 (smallest element containing x).
- For x ∈ T, let A(x) be smallest in Φ and B(x) smallest in Ψ.
- T is Φ-closed, so A(x) ⊂ T; likewise B(x) ⊂ T.
- By (c), A(x) ∈ Ψ, hence B(x) ⊂ A(x). Symmetrically B(x) ∈ Φ, hence A(x) ⊂ B(x).
- So C = A(x) = B(x) is the smallest member of Φ∪Ψ containing x.
- For x in only one of the supports, the smallest member is the obvious one.

c ⇒ a, step 2 (non-empty open parts). It remains to show that for A ∈ Φ∪Ψ the union of the members of Φ∪Ψ strictly contained in A is not A. Grothendieck reduces this to showing that Φ is closed in Φ∪Ψ (and Ψ likewise), which is done on p. 9.
errors: No substantive error. The step 'A ⊂ ∪B implies A ⊂ some B' silently uses A° ≠ ∅ (admissibility) and minimality of A(x) for x ∈ A°. This is valid but not written out.
The page is a heavily crossed-out draft. The final line of the b⇒c argument as written ('Ψ fermé dans Ψ') is a slip for 'Φ∩Ψ fermé dans Φ'.
In c⇒a, the case x ∈ |Φ| \ |Ψ| (and symmetrically) is not treated explicitly. It is trivial.

ideas.what: Admissible families of subsets: each point has a smallest member containing it, and each member has a non-empty 'open part' A°. These are equivalent to a stratification indexed by a poset, with members as closures of strata.
ideas.modern_name: Face poset of a stratified space / Alexandrov (finite T0) topology; poset-stratified sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (1937) for poset topologies; stratified spaces: Whitney, Thom, Mather; face posets of regular cell complexes (folklore)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses tame topology and stratified structures but not this formalism

ideas.what: Compatibility criterion for gluing two admissible families along a common closed sub-family (the equivalent conditions a, b, c).
ideas.modern_name: Gluing / pushout of posets (or cell complexes) along a common downset (subcomplex)

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary set-theoretic/combinatorial lemma on gluing poset-stratified families along closed subfamilies. It is correct and carefully done, but routine and close to folklore on face posets and Alexandrov topologies. Of mild historical interest only as part of Grothendieck's 1986 'algèbre des figures' foundations.
transcription_corrections: Line after 'on conclut A∈Ψ, q.e.d.': '$\Psi$ fermé dans $\Psi$' should read '(comme $\Phi\cap\Psi$ fermé dans $\Phi$)'. This is a parenthetical justification, not a new statement.
Around the 'Comme T=|Φ|∩|Ψ| est' line: the text is 'et itou soit B(x) le plus petit élément de Ψ tel que x∈B(x). Comme T=|Φ|∩|Ψ| est Φ-fermé dans |Φ|, on a A(x)⊂T, et de même (par c)) B(x)⊂T.'
'donc par définition' should likely read 'On doit donc avoir (par c)) A(x)∈Ψ, i.e. B(x)⊂A(x), et de même B(x)∈Φ i.e. A(x)⊂B(x)'.
'Cela montre que C est le plus petit' refers to C = A(x) = B(x).
The last lines read approximately: 'Il suffit pour ceci de prouver que si A∈Φ, les B ⊂ A (B∈Φ∪Ψ) sont dans Φ'. This anticipates p. 9: 'Φ fermé dans Φ∪Ψ'.
The '$\Psi$' in '$A\in\Psi$' of the b⇒c conclusion is correct. The crossed-out passage concerns applying the reasoning to B.
